clue.text: Philosophical doctrine is taken to be a field of interest

indicators.note: taken means removed, so the word is comes out of the doctrine's name

parts.note: realism is the philosophical doctrine that the world exists independently of the mind
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school of philosophy is treated as a whole area of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' removes IS from REALISM, leaving the shorter word; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a sphere or domain, as in the realm of science, so it means a field of interest.

clue.text: Verdict is given anew, getting one imprisoned?

definitions.text: Verdict is given anew, getting one imprisoned?

indicators.note: imprisoned means the single letter is locked inside the rearranged letters
given anew says the letters of the two words are delivered again in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A court verdict is retried, and somebody ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given anew' rearranges VERDICTIS to RECDIVIST, and 'imprisoned' puts I inside it. The whole clue also hints at the answer: a person given a verdict again who gets locked up again.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat offender keeps being convicted and jailed afresh, which is just what the clue describes.

clue.text: Girl yawning, regularly dropping off

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word yawning, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A young woman yawns again and again as she nods off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'yawning'; 'dropping off' just finishes the sleepy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a common female first name, so it fits the general word girl.

clue.text: Like a sort of fast day when detective loses time

definitions.text: Like a sort of fast day

indicators.note: loses means the letter for time drops out of the detective's name

parts.note: Maigret is the Paris police detective in Georges Simenon's novels

explanation.surface: On a day of fasting a detective finds himself losing track of the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A maigre day is one in the Catholic calendar when meat is not eaten, a kind of fast day.

clue.text: Dealership the man's established in foreign country

indicators.note: established in means set up inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: France is a country foreign to the British setter
his means belonging to the man

explanation.surface: A man has set up a car dealership abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licence to sell a company's goods, so it is a kind of dealership.

clue.text: Bachelorhood in Maryland?

parts.note: an unmarried man is in a ..., and the Old Line State of Maryland also has a nickname meaning the same

explanation.definitionFit: Maryland is nicknamed the Free State, and a bachelor's condition is one of being free, unattached.

clue.text: Succeeded in an eleven, finally out stumped

parts.note: an gives the single letter A

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the other letters
finally out means the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: a cricket or football eleven is a team
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: A batsman's side did well, but in the end he was out stumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' looks like cricket, a game of elevens, but it means baffled. 'finally out' removes the last letter of the team, and 'in' puts S inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at sea is an idiom for being confused or baffled, just as stumped means puzzled.

clue.text: Manage to pen a couple of lines —- source of inspiration?

annotationWithheld.why: Manage to pen a couple of lines -- source of inspiration? (8): C(A,LL,I)OPE needs I from 'source of inspiration', which is also the definition (the Muse): one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Manage to pen a couple of lines —- source of inspiration?

clue.text: I look to collect writers on love —- here's a particular poem

indicators.note: to collect means to gather other letters inside

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts one piece above the next

parts.note: pens are writing instruments, so writers
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A man looks over a collection of love poets and picks out one poem in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Il Penseroso is a specific poem by John Milton, the companion piece to L'Allegro.

clue.text: Religious woman's movement going round in circles

definitions.meaning: Mary Baker ... founded the Christian Science church
a whirlpool or circular current of water or air

explanation.surface: A woman's faith group seems to be getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's joins the two meanings; the surface reads 'movement' as a religious organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is water or air swirling round, and Mrs Eddy was the founder of a religion.

clue.text: Prison numbers finally doubled —- good judgement?

parts.note: can is slang for prison
nines are numbers
the final letter of the numbers is written a second time

explanation.surface: Inmates' numbers are doubled in the end, which some call a sensible decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Canniness is shrewdness, careful good sense in practical matters.

clue.text: Fatty stuff in fleshy part I had reduced

parts.note: the lip is a fleshy part of the mouth
I had shortened to the contraction I'd

explanation.surface: Someone has cut down the fat on a fleshy part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipid is a fat or fatty substance, in chemical terms.

clue.text: To find a tree —- so tricky when there's this?

definitions.text: To find a tree —- so tricky when there's this?

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are juggled into a new order

explanation.surface: It is hard to find a tree once the forest has been cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges TOFINDATREESO, and the whole clue also describes the result: with the woods cut down, a tree is hard to find.
explanation.definitionFit: Deforestation is the clearing of trees, which leaves few to be found.

clue.text: Gen about bill, Conservative legislation favouring workers

indicators.note: about means going round, so the facts surround the other pieces

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the facts
AC is short for account, a bill
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Information about a bill shows Conservative laws helping the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gen' is British slang for information; 'about' has it go round the bill and the Tory, splitting after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Factory Acts were nineteenth-century British laws protecting factory workers.

clue.text: Conduct of your writer after drink, sunk in depression

indicators.note: sunk in means placed inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression

indicators.note: after puts the writer's word behind the drink

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
your writer is the setter, so me

explanation.surface: The writer's behaviour after a drink is to sink into gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low mood, but it is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is the way a person carries and conducts themselves.

clue.text: Evil number two may have a powerful grip

definitions.meaning: a bench tool with jaws for clamping work tight

explanation.surface: A wicked deputy holds on tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice means wickedness, a deputy (vice-chair) and a gripping clamp, three senses of one word.

clue.text: Do act to entertain the guests?

definitions.text: Do act to entertain the guests?

parts.words: Do act to entertain the guests?
parts.note: a do is a party, and a routine someone performs to amuse people at one

explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is a short act someone performs to entertain others at social gatherings.

clue.text: One way to get eight in small Caribbean dwelling

definitions.meaning: in US and West Indian usage, a small or insignificant building

explanation.surface: A small island home somehow adds up to eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the two meanings. The Concise Oxford gives the second sense as US and West Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times four equals eight, and the term is also West Indian slang for a cramped little building.

clue.text: Wise guy packing in group for nostalgic period on rail way

indicators.note: packing means holding inside, so the group goes within the wise man

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a team is a group

explanation.surface: A clever man fills a group with longing for the old railway days.
explanation.definitionFit: The steam age is the era of steam locomotives, remembered fondly by rail enthusiasts.

clue.text: Hospital in animated protest to bring necessary improvement

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the rearranged ones
animated suggests lively movement, so these letters are stirred

explanation.surface: Hospital staff protest vigorously to force much-needed change.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop the rot is an idiom for halting a decline, bringing badly needed improvement.

clue.text: Characters inside school getting cooked salmon

indicators.note: cooked means messed with, so the letters are rearranged
characters inside means the letters within the word, leaving out its first and last

explanation.surface: Pupils in a school are served a cooked salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: The coho is a species of Pacific salmon.

clue.text: Black tree with less growth on

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A dark tree has fewer leaves on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Balder means having less hair, so less growth on the head.

clue.text: Repeatedly following a possible pattern for 1 dn?

definitions.meaning: over and over, again and again
1 down is a repeat offender, whose life might be a cycle of a spell in prison and then a spell free

explanation.surface: A habitual criminal keeps following the same pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' joins the two meanings. 1 down's answer is the habitual offender, in jail one period and out the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Year in, year out is an idiom meaning continually, every year without change.

clue.text: Less resting like this could make one happy

definitions.text: Less resting like this could make one happy

parts.words: Less resting like this could make one happy
parts.note: put the word less resting inside a bed and you get a word meaning happy or fortunate

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: LESS placed in BED gives BLESSED, which means happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as instructions, the answer puts LESS within BED to make a word meaning happy.

clue.text: Pledge of marriage given in writing

definitions.meaning: a suitor asks for a woman's ..., her promise to marry

explanation.surface: A promise to marry is put down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given in' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand means a promise to marry and also a person's handwriting.

clue.text: Variable current with only half the sailors getting to a port

parts.note: AC is alternating current, which keeps changing direction

indicators.note: only half means the second half of the word for sailors is dropped

parts.note: the crew are a ship's sailors

explanation.surface: A shifting current leaves a ship short-handed on its way to harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps CR from CREW; 'getting to' joins it to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital and chief port of Ghana.

clue.text: Attack brings retreat of men in lousy team

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the bad team

parts.note: lousy means bad

indicators.note: retreat means going backwards, so the letters for men are read in reverse

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A poor team's men fall back while under attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lousy' tempts as an anagram signal, but it is simply bad. 'retreat of' turns the men backwards before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a firing of all guns on one side of a ship, or any fierce verbal attack.

clue.text: It's a Gershwin song, beginning to end

indicators.note: beginning to end means the first letter is moved to the back

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A Gershwin tune that opens where it finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George Gershwin.

clue.text: Bit of letter not visible here

definitions.text: Bit of letter not visible here

parts.words: Bit of letter not visible here
parts.note: a part of some letters that drops below the line, and none of the letters in this very clue have one

explanation.walkthrough: Look at the clue: none of its letters (no g, j, p, q or y) dips below the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A descender is the stroke of a letter such as g or y that extends below the baseline.

clue.text: Joint by river is where they hold hops

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops, found in oast houses in Kent

explanation.surface: A pub by the river is where hops are stored.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven.
